messages:
ashley: Quick idea — propose an "opaque weight proxy" as a streaming sandbox between storage and runtime. It validates/normalizes formats (safetensors, tar/gz, blobs) and exposes a tiny, uniform shard streaming API so the runtime doesn't have to implement every loader variant.

michael: Curious — why opaque vs index-first? How does this change warmup semantics?

ashley: Two goals: decouple runtime from format parsing, and enable progressive hydration + integrity checks without coupling format impls into runtime. Also lets us do per-shard auth/throttling and incremental repairs.

priya: Sounds promising. How would the handshake look? Inline index or sidecar manifest?

ashley: Proxy exposes a small manifest endpoint e.g. GET /v1/shard/{id}/meta returning JSON segments with byte ranges, checksums, and optional routing hints. Runtime uses Range requests to pull normalized chunks. If there's no manifest, proxy synthesizes one on first access (cheap on-demand index).

sam: Won't this add latency on cold-starts? Warmup needs low latency for hot shards.

ashley: We plan a warmup fast-path: runtime can POST /v1/warmup with shard list + priority; proxy can serve a consolidated prefix bundle (pre-indexed cache) plus an early-KV block so runtime can populate KV cache quickly. Pin first N segments for hot shards.

luis: Where does the index live? In proxy memory or external store?

ashley: Hybrid: small in-memory LRU for hot models, plus a persistent index in RocksDB/metadata store for long-tail. Index entries canonicalize by checksum so multiple manifests can point to same physical object.

michael: Security: will proxy see plaintext weights? KMS/HSM integration?

ashley: Modes: 1) fully-trusted proxy (Dedicated/Private) decrypts with KMS and serves normalized chunks; 2) passthrough mode where proxy acts as a validator (verifies signatures/checksums) but doesn't keep plaintext (BYOK flow). We can integrate with customer CMK for hosted KMS flows.

priya: What about safetensors zero-copy mmap? Proxy would prevent zero-copy unless it forwards file descriptor — that kills perf if we always stream.

ashley: Agree. We'll have an optimized local pass-through: when storage is co-located with runtime (same node or NFS), proxy can return a v2 header that includes a handle for zero-copy (unix domain socket ancillary fd transfer) or a signed path for local open. For cloud blob storage we stream.

sam: Fallbacks for partial corruption? We need to avoid noisy failures mid-warmup.

ashley: Proxy does segment-level checksums and can attempt repairs by fetching alternate replica or a delta/gzip fallback shard. If repair fails, proxy returns a structured error (4xx) with a "fallback:variant" header so routing layer can route to a smaller model variant gracefully.

priya: How do we handle sharded layout changes (v1 -> v2 bundle formats)?

ashley: Versioned manifests. Proxy translates older manifests into the v2 canonical view on the fly. Migration tooling will populate translation caches. Runtime only sees the canonical manifest, so old bundles remain supported.

michael: How does warmup interplay with eviction and contention across models?

ashley: Warmup is hint-based. /v1/warmup accepts priority/ttl and a list of segments. Proxy has a global fetch queue with concurrency caps and backpressure. If runtime evicts, it sends a cancel or demote, and proxy lowers priority. Proxy also exposes SSE progress so runtime can reconcile.

luis: This adds infra surface — more services to run and instrument. Ops burden might be nontrivial.

ashley: True. Make proxy optional per deployment. Hosted will run a multi-tenant proxy for bandwidth/validation benefits. Dedicated/private can run a slim collocated proxy (local mode) or bypass it entirely for maximal perf.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: weight-proxy v0.1 to staging 2026-03-28 02:00 UTC

sam: One more: on-the-wire compression negotiation — we should support pre-compressed segments to save bandwidth in some regions.

ashley: Yes — Accept-Encoding negotiation and content-encoding for segments. Proxy can store/serve pre-compressed variants and honor client preferences, or decode server-side if the runtime asks for raw bytes.

priya: Any open risks we should call out in the RFC?

michael: Complexity, potential perf regressions for streamed path vs direct mmap, new failure modes to debug (proxy-induced corruption/latency), and observability gaps across the proxy boundary.

ashley: Action items: write short RFC with handshake proto + error model; build POC server that serves safetensors and gzipped tar bundles via normalized manifest; perf plan for cold/warm start (+ zero-copy pass-through).

sam: I'll take POC server side.

luis: I'll own the perf harness (cold start, warm start, pass-through vs stream).

priya: I'll draft the RFC and put a design doc in the repo.

ashley: TL;DR: opaque weight proxy = format normalization + streaming + warmup hints + fast-path pass-through when local + security modes for hosted/ BYOK. Volunteers and concerns noted. :thumbsup:
